findings.name: Real Property Tax Exemption for 100% Disabled Veterans
findings.description: Virginia exempts from local real property tax the principal residence (dwelling plus up to one acre of land) of any veteran rated by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs as 100 percent service-connected, permanent, and total. An unmarried surviving spouse of a qualifying veteran who died on or after January 1, 2011 may continue to receive the exemption.
findings.value: 100% exemption from local real property tax on the qualifying dwelling and up to 1 acre of land
otherReqs: Property must be occupied as the veteran's principal place of residence
Applies for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2011
documentation: VA Summary of Benefits letter showing 100% service-connected, permanent, and total disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: any veteran who has been rated by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs or its successor agency pursuant to federal law to have a 100 percent service-connected, permanent, and total disability... The surviving spouse of a veteran eligible for the exemption set forth in this article shall also qualify for the exemption, so long as the death of the veteran occurs on or after January 1, 2011, and the surviving spouse does not remarry.

findings.name: Personal Property Tax Exemption for One Vehicle (100% Disabled Veterans)
findings.description: One motor vehicle (passenger car, pickup, or panel truck registered for personal use) owned and used primarily by a 100 percent service-connected, permanent, and total disabled veteran is exempt from local personal property tax. For married couples, either spouse holding the qualifying rating makes the vehicle eligible. The exemption ends when the veteran dies and does not carry over to a surviving spouse.
findings.value: 100% exemption from local personal property tax on one qualifying vehicle
otherReqs: Applies to only one vehicle per veteran
Vehicle must be a passenger car, pickup, or panel truck registered for personal use
Exemption expires on the veteran's death; does not pass to a surviving spouse
documentation: VA rating decision or Summary of Benefits letter showing 100% service-connected, permanent, and total disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: one motor vehicle owned and used primarily by or for a veteran of the Armed Forces of the United States or the Virginia National Guard who has been rated by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs or its successor agency pursuant to federal law with a 100 percent service-connected, permanent, and total disability shall be exempt from taxation... This exemption shall be applicable beginning on the date the motor vehicle is acquired or January 1, 2021, whichever is later... The exemption shall expire on the date of the disabled veteran's death and shall not be available for his surviving spouse.

findings.name: Virginia Military Survivors and Dependents Education Program (VMSDEP)
findings.description: VMSDEP waives tuition and mandatory fees for up to eight semesters at a Virginia public college, university, or Eastern Virginia Medical School for the spouse or a child (ages 16-29) of a veteran who has been rated by the U.S. VA as totally and permanently disabled, or at least 90 percent permanently disabled, due to service, and discharged under conditions other than dishonorable (also available to survivors of service members killed, missing in action, or POW). Domicile/residency conditions apply to the qualifying service member. A separate stipend fund exists under Va. Code § 23.1-608.1, which was not independently verified in this research.
findings.value: Full waiver of tuition and mandatory fees for up to 8 semesters (4 academic years) at a Virginia public institution of higher education
otherReqs: Beneficiary is the spouse or a child aged 16-29 of the qualifying veteran or service member
Veteran discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable

Qualifying service member/veteran must meet Virginia domicile requirements (e.g., established residency at time of entering active service, or 5 years' physical presence in Virginia prior to application)
documentation: VA rating decision showing total/permanent disability or at least 90% permanent disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: a veteran who served in the Armed Forces of the United States, Reserves of the Armed Forces of the United States, or Virginia National Guard and, due to such service, has been rated by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs as totally and permanently disabled or at least 90 percent permanently disabled and has been discharged or released under conditions other than dishonorable... waiving tuition and mandatory fees at a public institution of higher education... Benefits are available for up to eight semesters, the equivalent of four academic years.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran (DV) License Plates
findings.description: Veterans with a service-connected disability certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs may obtain special red/white/blue 'DV' license plates. One set of Disabled Veteran or standard passenger special plates is provided at no cost to a veteran who has lost, or lost the use of, a limb, is blind, or is permanently and totally disabled (and to their un-remarried surviving spouse); other service-connected disabled veterans may purchase the DV plate design. The disabled (International Symbol of Access) version requires additional medical certification.
findings.value: Special DV-design license plate; free for veterans who lost/lost use of a limb, are blind, or are permanently and totally disabled
otherReqs: Certification from the U.S. VA that the disability is service-connected
Free set of plates limited to veterans who lost/lost use of a limb, are blind, or are permanently and totally disabled (or their un-remarried surviving spouse)
findings.form: VSA 10 (License Plate Application); VSA 54 (Veteran Certification of Disability)
documentation: Form VSA 54 signed by a veteran service officer, or a U.S. VA benefit letter
findings.sourceExcerpt: any veteran with a service-connected disability certified by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) may purchase Disabled Veteran special plates... either a signed Certificate of Disability (form VSA 54) signed by a veteran service officer or a U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs benefit letter

findings.name: Vehicle Registration Fee Waiver for Disabled Veterans
findings.description: No annual DMV registration fee is required for one motor vehicle owned and used personally by a veteran whose disability has been certified as service-connected by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. This waiver applies alongside (but is distinct from) the DV license plate program.
findings.value: Annual vehicle registration fee waived for one qualifying vehicle
otherReqs: Certification from the U.S. VA that the disability is service-connected
Limited to one motor vehicle owned and used personally by the veteran
documentation: Form VSA 54 or U.S. VA benefit letter certifying service-connected disability
findings.sourceExcerpt: No annual registration fee, as prescribed in § 46.2-694, and no annual fee...shall be required [for disabled veterans displaying special plates or standard passenger plates]... The application shall be accompanied by a certification from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs that the veteran's disability is service-connected.

findings.name: Veterans Preference in Commonwealth State Employment
findings.description: Veterans, their surviving spouses, and children receive hiring preference for Commonwealth of Virginia state government jobs. For positions using a numerically scored assessment, 5 percentage points are added to a veteran's passing score, or 10 points for a veteran with a service-connected disability rating fixed by the U.S. VA. For non-exam-based hiring, qualifying veterans, surviving spouses, or children are given preference in the selection process provided they meet all knowledge, skill, and ability requirements.
findings.value: 5-point score preference on scored exams (10 points for service-connected disabled veterans); preference in non-exam hiring
otherReqs: Honorable discharge and more than 180 consecutive days of full-time active-duty service, OR a service-connected disability rating fixed by the U.S. VA
Must meet all knowledge, skill, and ability requirements for the position
findings.agency: Virginia Department of Human Resource Management (DHRM)
documentation: VA disability rating letter, if claiming disability-based preference
findings.sourceExcerpt: any person who has received an honorable discharge and (i) has provided more than 180 consecutive days of full-time, active-duty service in the armed forces of the United States or reserve components thereof, including the National Guard, or (ii) has a service-connected disability rating fixed by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs... the veteran, surviving spouse, or child, shall be given preference by the Commonwealth during the selection process, provided that the veteran, surviving spouse, or child, meets all of the knowledge, skill, and ability requirements.

findings.name: Virginia Veterans Care Centers
findings.description: The Virginia Department of Veterans Services operates state veterans care centers providing skilled nursing, dementia/memory care, and short-term rehabilitative care, statutorily authorized as part of DVS's responsibility for 'medical care centers...for veterans owned and operated by the Commonwealth.' Publicly known locations include Sitter & Barfoot (Richmond), Davis & McDaniel (Roanoke), and Jones & Cabacoy (Virginia Beach), with a fourth (Puller, Fauquier County) reported as under construction. This research could not independently confirm the specific admission criteria (discharge type, minimum service length, income/means testing) or payer details because DVS's dedicated care-center and eligibility pages returned an access-blocked (HTTP 403) response on every direct fetch attempt; contact DVS or a specific care center to confirm current admission requirements before relying on any percentage or dollar figure.
